tasks.short: Judge where the company stands and where the month is heading.

today.trigger: More than weekly, and again when a site, a large customer or the Rabobank balance looks off.
steps: Pull actuals from the Power BI dashboards on the nightly AFAS extract: revenue, margin, labour, flex and cash by site.
Add Rabobank balances, unpaid agency invoices and open customer items that the dashboards show late or not at all.
Ask the controller and the two FP&A analysts for the bridge from last forecast to this week.
Write a short status for the management team: what changed, what it means for the month, what is still soft.
Sit in the management discussion and defend the outlook.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same site bridge in Excel because the Power BI page is a day behind or grouped wrong.
Chasing three agency portals and an inbox for flex cost that is not in AFAS yet.
Rewriting commentary that only restates the variance table.
today.time_sinks: About three hours a cycle goes to collecting figures that already exist in AFAS, Power BI or the bank, then making them agree.

lenses.faster: The pack and the first bridge are ready when the nightly extract lands, so the director starts at the judgment. Collecting and reconciling the standard tables disappears.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled run after the AFAS refresh builds the status and mails it when cash, site margin or flex cost crosses a set band, with no calendar reminder.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would want a weekly outlook by site, customer and labour type, including flex, that operations accept as the working forecast.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the spreadsheet chase. What remains is the conversation about whether Venlo or a large shipper is actually turning.
lenses.options: Each pack carries a base, a soft-volume and a high-flex case, with the cash and margin effect of each, instead of one commentary line.
lenses.altitude: The director sets the definitions, the thresholds and the sign-off rule, and reviews the packs that break the rule.
reach: The FP&A analyst's first variance note.
The controller's flash result once the subledgers are in.
A one-page factual note for the works council when the figures are ones the OR is entitled to see.

tasks.human_edge: The director is the person the management team holds responsible for the outlook. Calling a soft week noise, or the start of a bad quarter, depends on customer and site context that is not all in the ledger.
tasks.pattern_why: The status uses several systems and a draft narrative, and it counts only when the director releases it. A wrong outlook would break the forecast the business is asked to trust.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract and the latest Rabobank balance have landed, on the normal twice-weekly rhythm or when a threshold breaks.
steps: A job reads the extract, open debtors, open creditors and the flex-invoice accrual.
It builds the site bridge against the live forecast and drafts three short causes for each material line.
Exceptions (late agency invoices, uncoded cash, a site off by more than the band) are listed separately from settled figures.
The director edits the outlook, picks the case the management team will use, and releases the note.
Released packs are stored with the forecast version they refer to.
in_practice.human_gate: The director releases every status note before the management team or the works council relies on it.
data_needed: AFAS actuals by site, cost centre and period
The current forecast version
Rabobank balances and the facility limit
Open debtor and creditor totals
Agency hours and invoices not yet in AFAS
Thresholds agreed with the management team
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint finance library, folder Forecast / status log, with the AFAS period and forecast version in the file name.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit and a nightly Power BI extract already hold the actuals this status is built from.
Microsoft Copilot in Excel can draft a first variance comment from a table a person then checks.
A gated weekly pack for a three-site logistics firm would still need a person to judge late flex cost and the outlook.

risks: The nightly extract is stale for same-day cash and for agency invoices that arrive in lumps.
A fluent cause-of-variance sentence can name the wrong customer or site and still look tidy.
If the works council receives a softer summary than the management team, the OR information right is not met.
research_questions: What share of the current status is already a Power BI page the director trusts without an Excel rebuild?
After the nightly refresh, which lines still move because of agency invoices, accruals or bank items not yet in AFAS?
Which three questions does the management team always ask, and are the answers in AFAS or only in someone's head?

tasks.short: Decide customer credit limits and review financing requests.

today.trigger: A new customer, an order above the open limit, or a Rabobank or lease request the company itself wants to make.
steps: Read the request and the customer's payment history in AFAS.
Look up disputes, overdue items and any credit-insurance cover the credit officer holds.
For a new name, read the KvK extract and any accounts the salesperson sent by mail.
Compare the ask with the limit the director last approved for a similar customer.
Approve, cut or refuse, and tell the credit and collections officer what to record.
For a facility or lease, read the Rabobank or lessor term sheet and the effect on cash and the monthly result.
drudgery: Searching the inbox for the last promise a customer made.
Re-keying figures from a PDF of accounts into a side calculation.
Repeating the same limit check the credit officer could have finished inside a written matrix.
today.time_sinks: Daily requests queue behind meeting days, so sales waits on a limit that is often a repeat of last month's decision.

lenses.faster: Payment history, overdue, disputes and insurance cover arrive as one page. The director only opens the file when the matrix cannot decide.
lenses.autonomous: An order that would break the limit, or a new debtor in AFAS, opens a case on its own. In-policy repeats are recorded without a reminder.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would score every customer twice a year, and every peak-season flex in cash terms, which it now does only when someone asks.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses retyping PDF accounts. The work people want is the few limits that are really a bet on a shipper.
lenses.options: Each exception shows three limits: insure-and-cap, match the insurance cover, and the commercial ask, with bad-debt and revenue next to each.
lenses.altitude: The director maintains the matrix, the euro threshold and the rule for sole traders, and reviews breaches and a sample of automatic limits.
reach: The credit and collections officer's routine limit checks.
The bookkeeper's block on orders once a limit is fully used.
A first read of a Rabobank or lease term sheet before the management team sees it.

tasks.human_edge: Granting terms beyond policy to a shipper the company wants, or refusing one, is a commercial and bad-debt call. A sole trader is a natural person: a fully automatic refusal would sit under AVG article 22 and the EU AI Act credit rules.
tasks.pattern_why: Most inputs are structured debtor data and a written matrix, with a document step for new accounts. The limit counts in AFAS only after the rule is met or the director signs an exception.

in_practice.trigger: A new debtor, an order above the open limit, or a financing term sheet saved to SharePoint.
steps: The job pulls AFAS payment days, overdue, disputes and the current limit.
It extracts key figures from any KvK extract or accounts PDF and fills the same checklist.
Inside the matrix, it records the limit and writes the reason on the debtor.
Outside the matrix, or for any natural person, it sends the case to the director with three options.
The director's decision is written back to AFAS by the credit officer.
in_practice.human_gate: The director decides every exception, every natural person, and every company facility or lease. In-policy company limits are sampled, not signed one by one.
data_needed: Debtor payment history, overdue and disputes in AFAS
Written limit matrix and euro threshold
Credit-insurance cover where the company holds it
KvK number and, for new customers, accounts
A flag for natural persons and eenmanszaken
Facility and lease term sheets
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS debtor dossier, plus a credit-decision list on the SharePoint finance site.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit stores debtor limits, open items and payment history that a limit check can read.
Atradius and Allianz Trade already supply trade-credit opinions and cover used by Dutch firms.
A policy matrix can clear repeat buyers; new names and sole traders still need a person.

risks: Promises and disputes that live in Outlook are invisible, so the matrix looks safer than the book.
Automated decisions on sole traders can breach AVG article 22 and, from August 2026, high-risk rules in the EU AI Act.
A limit written in AFAS is a commercial commitment; a wrong automatic raise is hard to walk back with a large shipper.
research_questions: How many limit decisions are there each month, and what share already follow a written matrix?
What share of applicants are natural persons or eenmanszaken?
Is payment behaviour complete in AFAS, or do promises and disputes sit in mail and the credit officer's notes?
Does a credit insurer already set a cover that finance only copies into AFAS?

tasks.short: See who owes us and whether collection is on track.

today.trigger: More than weekly, and whenever a large shipper goes past the agreed days.
steps: Run the AFAS debtor aging and export it to Excel.
Strip unapplied cash, inter-site noise and items the credit officer has already marked as disputed.
Compare the total with last week's forecast for receipts.
Read the credit officer's notes on the largest overdue names.
Decide which accounts need a director and which stay with the officer.
drudgery: Rebuilding the aging because dispute codes and unapplied cash are messy.
Adding up the same top-20 customers every week.
Copying the officer's mail notes into the sheet so the meeting has one list.
today.time_sinks: Most of the hour is cleaning the aging into a status, not deciding what to do.

lenses.faster: The status is the exception list: broken promises, disputes over a set amount, and overdue that changed the DSO forecast. Preparing the full aging by hand disappears.
lenses.autonomous: After each nightly AFAS refresh the list rebuilds itself, and a Teams note fires only when collectible overdue crosses the band.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would forecast receipts by week and by customer, and would see DSO by site every morning in peak season.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the export cleanup. The useful remainder is the judgment on a strategic customer who is late.
lenses.options: The list shows, for each large item, collect, dispute, payment plan or credit-note, with the effect on the month's cash.
lenses.altitude: The director sets what counts as collectible, disputed and escalated, and reviews the definition when DSO and cash diverge.
reach: The credit and collections officer's daily chase list.
The bookkeeper's unapplied-cash queue.
The FP&A receipt line in the weekly cash forecast.

tasks.human_edge: When a strategic shipper is late because of a service failure at a site, the next step is a management conversation, not another reminder. The director owns that call.
tasks.pattern_why: Open items, due dates, dispute flags and cash application are structured AFAS data. The status is a set of rules with a checkable total back to the debtor ledger.

in_practice.trigger: Each morning after the AFAS refresh, and at once when a named account or the overdue total crosses the threshold.
steps: The job ages open items and splits them into collectible, disputed, unapplied cash and promised.
It ties the total to the AFAS debtor control account and stops if the tie fails.
It compares expected receipts with the forecast and flags the names that explain the gap.
The credit officer works the list. The director sees only escalations and the weekly cash effect.
Actions are written back as AFAS notes so the next run does not raise the same item.
in_practice.human_gate: The director acts on escalations and on any change to a provision. The officer owns the rest. A broken tie to the ledger blocks the list.
data_needed: Open debtor items with due date, site and customer
Dispute and promise codes
Unapplied cash
Debtor control-account balance
The receipt line in the cash forecast
Escalation thresholds
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS collection notes on the debtor, and a weekly overdue snapshot in the SharePoint finance library.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit produces debtor aging, open items and a debtor control account that a status list can tie to.
Credit-management products such as Onguard already turn open items into worklists for Dutch collection teams.
Where dispute status lives only in mail, an aging rule will overstate what is collectible until the codes are kept in AFAS.

risks: Items coded as collectible that are really service disputes inflate the cash forecast.
A director who stops looking at the full book can miss a slow slide in a mid-sized customer.
Chasing letters generated from a stale code can breach the tone agreed with a key shipper.
research_questions: What share of overdue euros is a coded dispute or unapplied cash, rather than a customer who has not paid?
Does the nightly aging match what the credit officer calls collectible, within a tolerance finance would sign?
How often does the director's review change the next action, rather than confirm what the officer already knew?

tasks.short: Prepare the board pack and the reports the law requires.

today.trigger: Month close, the BTW period, the annual jaarrekening, a board meeting, and information the works council must receive.
steps: Wait until the controller locks the AFAS period and the main reconciliations are done.
Pull the statements and the management bridge from AFAS and Power BI into the board pack.
Draft the commentary, the cash note and the points that need a decision.
Prepare or review the BTW return, the annual accounts file and the KvK filing with the controller.
Send the OR the financial information the WOR requires, in line with the board figures.
Sign what the law or the bank puts on the director, after the auditor's points are in.
drudgery: Copying ledgers into a slide or Word table that breaks when a late journal posts.
Chasing tie-outs between the board pack, the BTW working paper and the annual-accounts file.
Formatting appendices the board does not read.
today.time_sinks: Days bunch at close. A large part is waiting for agency accruals, then reformatting numbers that already tie.

lenses.faster: Once the period is locked, the statements, the bridge and a first management commentary are already in the pack. Re-keying and formatting drop out.
lenses.autonomous: The close checklist, not a reminder, starts the pack when the controller marks the period ready, and again on the BTW and jaarrekening dates.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would keep an audit-ready file every month, and would give the OR and the board the same numbers without a separate scramble.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the format work. The part worth keeping is the judgment on provisions, claims and what the board is asked to decide.
lenses.options: Late adjustments are shown as scenarios: book now, disclose only, or leave as a post-balance event, with the effect on result and covenants.
lenses.altitude: The director designs the pack, the tie-out list and the judgment log, and stops building the tables.
reach: The controller's statutory lead sheets and SBR mapping checks.
The accountant's BTW working paper, as a review rather than a preparation.
The factual financial note for the works council.

tasks.human_edge: The signature on the jaarrekening, the tax position and any bank certificate stays with management. Provisions for claims, flex-cost cut-off and going concern are judgments the auditor will ask a person to explain.
tasks.pattern_why: The numbers come from a locked ledger and a checklist, and the words can be drafted. Each filing and each board pack counts only after the director approves it, because the liability sits there.

in_practice.trigger: The controller sets the AFAS period to ready for reporting, or a statutory date (BTW, jaarrekening, KvK, board, OR) is inside the preparation window.
steps: The job checks the tie-out list: subledgers, bank, BTW, payroll control account, agency accrual.
It fills the board pack and the accounts tables from the locked period.
It drafts commentary only from variances that tie to a ledger line, and leaves a blank where they do not.
The director and the controller review judgments, related items and the OR text.
Filing and sending wait for that sign-off. The SBR file is submitted by the controller after approval.
in_practice.human_gate: The director approves every board pack, every OR financial note, the BTW return and the jaarrekening before they are sent or filed. Nothing is auto-filed.
data_needed: Locked AFAS period and trial balance
Reconciliation status for bank, debtors, creditors, BTW and payroll
Agency accrual basis
Prior-year comparatives and the RJ checklist the auditor uses
Rabobank facility terms if a certificate is required
The version of the figures already shared with the OR
in_practice.logs_to: The statutory dossier on SharePoint (jaarrekening and BTW), with the AFAS audit trail and a judgment log next to the board pack.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit produces the trial balance, VAT support and financial statements that Dutch filings start from.
Dutch annual accounts are filed through SBR via Digipoort to the Kamer van Koophandel and the Belastingdienst.
CaseWare and Silverfin are used in the Dutch market to assemble a statutory file and track review.
An auditor will still require a person to own the judgments, even when the tables tie.

risks: A drafted bestuursverslag can state a cause the ledger does not support, and the director may sign it under time pressure.
Auto-filing would put management signature on a return nobody opened.
The OR note and the board pack can drift apart if they are generated as two stories.
research_questions: Which of these reports does the director write today, and which does the controller already draft?
How many close days are lost to late subledgers and agency invoices, and how many to commentary and formatting?
Will the external auditor rely on drafted lead sheets if every figure ties to AFAS and the judgment log is signed?
Is the SBR mapping from AFAS stable from last year's filing?

tasks.short: Review finance routines and recommend what should change.

today.trigger: A weak close, an audit adjustment, a DSO jump, or a request from the management team to simplify a process.
steps: Pick one stream: procure to pay, order to cash, the close, or the forecast.
Pull touch rates, manual journals, days to close, DSO and the last audit points from AFAS and the close file.
Talk to the controller, the bookkeepers and the credit officer about where the work actually sticks.
Compare the written SharePoint procedure with what people do in peak season.
Write a short recommendation: what to change, who owns it, what it does to the north-star measures.
If the change touches staff work or monitoring, prepare the point for works-council advice.
drudgery: Reading old procedures that no longer match the AFAS setup.
Sampling invoices by hand to see how many posted without a touch.
Collecting examples so a recommendation is not only an opinion.
today.time_sinks: The evidence is scattered across AFAS workflow history, inboxes and a close folder, so a one-page recommendation takes days of digging.

lenses.faster: The evidence pack (touch rate, manual journals, close-day waterfall, DSO bridges, audit points) is ready before the director looks. The digging steps shrink.
lenses.autonomous: A missed monthly target on days to close, touchless invoices, DSO or audit adjustments opens a review file on its own.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would review one control every month and would finally measure touchless invoices properly, which it only samples now.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses sampling invoices on a Friday. The good part is choosing a change the ten-person team can actually hold in peak season.
lenses.options: Each recommendation comes as three designs: an AFAS setting, a checklist change, and a staffing change, with effort and effect on the north star.
lenses.altitude: This task is already the design layer. AI does the measurement; the director decides what the system should become.
reach: The controller's process notes for the close.
The bookkeepers' payment and coding rules.
A worked example for the works council when a change is an OR advice matter.

tasks.human_edge: The director chooses the order of change for a small team across three sites, and whether the OR must be asked. That is a judgment about people and risk, not about the table.
tasks.pattern_why: The class of this work is amplify: the director stays the author of the recommendation. AI prepares the evidence and the options; it does not issue the change.

in_practice.trigger: A month where days to close, forecast accuracy, DSO, touchless invoices or audit adjustments miss the agreed band, or a planned quarterly review.
steps: A job pulls the four measures and the manual-journal list from AFAS for the last six months.
It samples exceptions and attaches the underlying document link.
It drafts three options against the written procedure on SharePoint.
The director talks to the people who run the stream, cuts the options to one recommendation, and names an owner.
If the change processes employee data or monitors staff, the director routes it for OR advice before it is built.
in_practice.human_gate: The director signs every recommendation. No AFAS setup, role or procedure changes on the back of an unsigned draft.
data_needed: Workflow history for purchase invoices and cash application
Manual journal log and close calendar
DSO by customer and site
Audit-adjustment list
The current procedure on SharePoint
Whether the change touches employee data or staff monitoring
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint finance library, folder Controls / recommendations, one note per review with the decision and the owner.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit logs invoice workflow, journals and debtor days that a touch-rate and close review can measure.
BlackLine and FloQast publish close-checklist and reconciliation status that finance teams use to see where a close sticks.
A recommendation that ignores peak-season flex volume or the works council will be agreed and then not used.

risks: A measure with a soft definition (what counts as a touch) produces a confident recommendation about the wrong problem.
Changes to how staff are monitored, or how their data feeds a finance check, can require works-council advice under WOR article 27.
The team can collect review packs and still not change AFAS.
research_questions: Is there a written close, credit and invoice procedure, or is the system the habits of the ten people?
Which recommendations from the last two years were implemented, and what blocked the rest?
Can touchless rate, days to close, DSO and audit adjustments be counted from AFAS without a new definition argument?

tasks.short: Prepare the risk and operations report for management.

today.trigger: Before each management-team meeting, and when a site, a claim or cash moves outside the usual band.
steps: Take the operational figures FP&A and the sites already use: volume, labour, flex, damage, penalties.
Add the finance reading: margin by site, debtor risk, cash, Rabobank headroom, open claims.
Ask site finance contacts or the controller which variances are one-offs.
Write a short risk list with an owner and a euro amount.
Put it in the management pack and walk through the red items.
drudgery: Aligning site spreadsheets with the AFAS cost centres.
Turning three agency hour files into one flex-cost risk line.
Rewriting last month's risk list because the file was copied forward.
today.time_sinks: The slow part is making one definition of margin, flex and claims that both finance and the sites will accept.

lenses.faster: The standard pages (site margin, flex versus plan, claims, debtors, cash, facility headroom) arrive tied to AFAS. Building them by export disappears.
lenses.autonomous: The report run starts from the management-meeting date and from any breach of a risk band, without someone remembering to start it.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would watch these risks weekly in peak season, including flex cover at each site, which it now sees once a month.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses merging agency files. What people value is a short red list the meeting will actually use.
lenses.options: Each red item shows a low, expected and high euro outcome for the quarter, and what would have to be true for the high case.
lenses.altitude: The director sets the risk taxonomy and the bands, and reviews the red list and any line that did not tie.
reach: The FP&A analyst's business-review pages.
The credit officer's debtor-risk paragraph.
A labour-cost risk line built from payroll totals, without opening individual absence files.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding which risks are material for this management team, and standing behind that list when a site manager disagrees, is the director's job.
tasks.pattern_why: The report pulls several sources, applies tie-out rules, and drafts the red list. Management uses it, so the director approves each edition before it is sent.

in_practice.trigger: Five working days before the management meeting, or a band breach on margin, claims, overdue or facility headroom.
steps: The job loads site actuals, flex accruals, open claims, debtor risk and the Rabobank balance.
It ties each page to AFAS and marks any figure that comes from outside the ledger.
It drafts the red list with an owner, an amount and three outcomes, and leaves a blank where the cause is not in the data.
The director cuts the list, checks anything outside the ledger, and releases the report.
The released file is the one FP&A is allowed to reuse in the forecast.
in_practice.human_gate: The director releases each management edition. Untied figures cannot be presented as ledger fact.
data_needed: Site profit and loss and volume from AFAS
Flex hours and invoices by site
Open claims and customer penalties
Debtor risk totals
Rabobank balance and facility limit
Agreed risk bands and owners
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint management-report folder, one released file per meeting, with the AFAS period on the cover.

evidence.claim: Power BI on an AFAS extract is already the company's channel for HR and finance dashboards, refreshed nightly.
A management risk page that mixes ledger totals with agency-portal hours can be produced reliably only if those hours are reconciled to invoices.

risks: Site managers keep a second set of operating figures, so a ledger-only risk list is disputed in the meeting and then ignored.
Individual absence or productivity detail would pull the report into AVG and works-council territory; the finance page needs totals.
An unreleased draft forwarded from Teams becomes the number the sites remember.
research_questions: Which risk lines did the management team act on in the last year, and which pages were never opened?
Do flex hours, claims and volume live in AFAS, or in site spreadsheets and the three agency portals?
If a wrong line is published, is the damage worse than a late line? That decides whether every edition needs a signature.

tasks.short: Use cost data to build the budget.

today.trigger: The budget round, a known CAO wage change, or a volume plan from operations that moves flex and labour.
steps: Take last year's AFAS actuals by site and cost centre and strip one-off items.
Apply the two wage paths: the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO, plus allowances and pension.
Add flex: a band of 150 to 300 agency workers, using the three agencies' rates and last season's hours.
Check purchased transport, housing, energy and damage against the volume plan.
Review the FP&A model, challenge the sites, and freeze the cost budget the forecast will use.
drudgery: Cleaning last year's actuals so one-off claims and late agency invoices do not become next year's base.
Rebuilding the flex bridge because the three agencies do not code sites the same way.
Version chaos in Excel when two FP&A analysts and the sites all edit.
today.time_sinks: The labour and flex bridge, not the housing and energy lines, takes most of the hours.

lenses.faster: The cost base, the CAO maths and the flex band are calculated before the first budget meeting. Cleaning actuals and re-keying rates drop out.
lenses.autonomous: A new CAO rate, or an operations volume plan that moves flex outside the band, rebuilds the cost case without waiting for the annual calendar.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would keep a rolling cost forecast by site and labour type, and would budget a peak season it currently only discovers in the agency invoice.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses mapping agency spreadsheets onto cost centres. The work people want is the argument with a site manager about a number both will live with.
lenses.options: Every round has at least three cost cases: CAO-only, base volume, and a high-flex peak, with cash and margin by site.
lenses.altitude: The director sets the cost definitions, the flex band and what may be reopened after freeze, and checks the cases rather than building them.
reach: The FP&A analysts' driver model.
The payroll specialist's CAO wage scenario, at cost-centre level.
The compensation specialist's input on allowances, taken as a rate table rather than a side mail.

tasks.human_edge: The budget is a commitment to site managers and to the management team. Choosing the flex band and the wage case, when commercial promises and the two CAOs do not match, stays with the director.
tasks.pattern_why: Cost actuals, wage tables and rate cards are structured enough to calculate. The budget counts only when the director and the management team adopt a named version.

in_practice.trigger: The budget calendar opens, a CAO wage table is updated on SharePoint, or the operations volume plan moves flex outside the agreed band.
steps: The job builds a cost base from AFAS actuals and flags one-off journals and late agency invoices.
It applies the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO tables, and the agency rate cards, to the volume plan.
It produces three cases by site and shows where a line does not tie to a source.
FP&A reviews the drivers with the sites. The director freezes one case.
The frozen version is the one the forecast and the board pack are allowed to use.
in_practice.human_gate: The director freezes the cost budget. Cases can be prepared without approval; they cannot enter the forecast before that freeze.
data_needed: AFAS actuals by site and cost centre, with one-off journals marked
Transport CAO and warehouse CAO wage tables and allowance rules
Agency rate cards and hour history by site
Operations volume plan
Payroll control totals, not individual absence files
The current forecast version
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint budget folder, one frozen version per round, referenced by the forecast and by AFAS budget entries.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit holds cost-centre actuals and payroll journals that a budget base can be built from.
CAO wage increases are table-driven once the agreement is known, so the arithmetic can be checked to the cent.
Excel and Power BI already do the last mile of this work in most Dutch mid-market finance teams.

risks: A base that treats last year's agency catch-up invoices as a run-rate will overstate next year's flex cost.
Using individual absence or poortwachter files to refine labour cost would breach data minimisation. Totals are enough.
Two CAO tables applied to the wrong population (drivers versus warehouse) silently moves the largest cost.
research_questions: What share of cost variance is the two CAOs plus flex, versus purchased transport, housing and energy?
Can agency hours and invoices be reconciled per site and week, or is flex still a lump sum?
Do site managers accept a budget built from AFAS actuals and CAO rates, or do they rebuild it in Excel anyway?

tasks.short: Check price lists and rates against margin and cash.

today.trigger: A new customer tariff, a carrier or agency price list, a diesel-surcharge change, or a change in the Rabobank rate.
steps: Save the list from mail into the contract folder on SharePoint.
Read the change: base rate, diesel clause, staangeld, agency fee or interest.
Compare it with the rate already in the forecast and in the customer or supplier agreement.
Work out the year effect on margin and, for interest, on cash.
Tell FP&A and, if it is material, the management team.
drudgery: Reading PDF rate cards and side letters that all use a different layout.
Re-doing the diesel-surcharge maths each time the reference price moves.
Hunting the current contractual rate because the forecast copy is old.
today.time_sinks: The time goes into finding the binding rate and turning a PDF into rows, not into the margin decision.

lenses.faster: A saved price list comes back as rows: rate, unit, surcharge, start date and euro effect. Re-keying and the first comparison disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A file added to the rate-card folder, or a known diesel reference move, starts the comparison without a reminder.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would check every carrier, agency and customer rate against margin every month, which it now does when a list happens to arrive.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses retyping tariffs. The useful remainder is the call on whether a surcharge is absorbed or reopened with the customer.
lenses.options: Each material change shows absorb, pass on, or reopen the contract, with margin and cash for the rest of the year.
lenses.altitude: The director sets which clauses matter, the euro threshold, and the rule that the forecast may use only registered rates.
reach: The FP&A update of the forecast rate.
Procurement's comparison of carrier tenders, as a finance check on margin.
The bookkeeper's check that an agency invoice uses the registered rate card.

tasks.human_edge: Whether to absorb a diesel or carrier increase, or to reopen a customer rate, is a commercial decision made with sales. Finance supplies the checked effect; it does not own the relationship.
tasks.pattern_why: Rate cards arrive as PDFs and mixed spreadsheets. The useful output is a structured table a person can tie back to the contract and to AFAS. The arithmetic after that is ordinary calculation.

in_practice.trigger: A rate card or term sheet is saved to the SharePoint contract folder, or the agreed diesel reference is updated.
steps: The job reads the file and extracts rate, unit, surcharge rule, start date and party.
A person checks the extracted rows against the PDF before they are stored.
The checked rows are compared with the forecast and with the last registered card.
Changes under the threshold update a watch list. Changes over it go to the director with three commercial options.
FP&A may change the forecast only from a registered card the director has released.
in_practice.human_gate: The director releases any rate change above the threshold before it enters the forecast or a customer position. Extraction errors are caught by the row check before that.
data_needed: Customer tariffs, carrier lists and the three agency rate cards
The diesel-surcharge clause and the reference series named in the contract
The rate version inside the live forecast
Rabobank interest terms
The euro threshold for escalation
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint rate-card register, one row per party and start date, linked to the forecast version.

evidence.claim: Once rates are rows, Excel or Power BI can compute a margin and cash effect and tie it to a forecast version.
Microsoft Document Intelligence can extract tables from PDFs into rows a person then checks.
Dutch side letters on dieseltoeslag and staangeld are often messy enough that unchecked extraction will misstate the year effect.

risks: A misread surcharge clause posts a clean-looking margin bridge that is wrong for the whole year.
This O*NET line may be almost empty here if the company holds no securities and commercial owners keep the price lists.
A forecast fed from an unchecked PDF becomes the number the board later calls forecast accuracy.
research_questions: Does the company hold securities, or only cash and a Rabobank facility? How many hours does this task really take?
Where do the binding price lists live, and what share are searchable text rather than scans or side letters?
How often does a rate-card change move margin by more than the threshold the director would act on?

role.altitude: The finance director stops assembling the month and becomes the person who designs the close, the forecast, the credit rules and the management pack, then checks the exceptions, the judgments and the signature items.
reach: The controller's close checklist, reconciliation status and statutory tie-out.
The FP&A analysts' first forecast pass and the site variance notes.
The credit and collections officer's in-policy limit checks and the weekly overdue list.
The bookkeepers' rules for supplier invoices that can post without a touch.
The payroll specialist's CAO wage scenarios, at cost-centre level only.
A factual financial note for the works council under the WOR information right.
role.ceiling_note: One director and nine specialists cover three sites. These eight tasks are about 43% of the year; the rest is the management team, the bank, the auditor, the works council and leading the team. Signatures, bad-news conversations and the forecast the business will believe stay with the person. The nightly AFAS extract sets the pace, and in peak season agency hours and invoices arrive late.
skills_to_grow: Read an AFAS extract and a Power BI model, and check a total with a simple SQL query against the ledger.
Write credit, close and forecast rules that a colleague and the auditor can re-perform.
Dutch reporting judgments under BW Title 9 and the RJ, and which ones the auditor will challenge.
Spot when a finance run touches personal data, a sole trader's credit, or the works council, and stop it.
Review machine output by sample, tie-out and log, rather than by reading every page.
role.ambitious_version: The month closes in three working days. A weekly forecast by site, customer and labour type, own staff and flex, is the one operations recognise as their numbers. Most supplier invoices post untouched. Overdue debt is an exception list with a named owner. The director's week goes to margin, the Rabobank facility, capex on the three sites, and the few judgments that change the year.
